payload.rebuttal: fixed: The probe's mutant (skip the depends_on cut whenever the text contains '&') survived because no draft in the witness carried an unreferenced anchor: the only '&' in the whole test was the alias draft's own dangling reference, which already pools for the same reason under both the real code and the mutant, so the two were indistinguishable. I added an anchor (&flow_deps) to the flow-form group's depends_on line with no alias anywhere else referencing it. The real code still cuts and mints that group normally, since removing the one line loses nothing. Under the mutant, the presence of '&' now skips the cut entirely, so that group pools instead of minting, and the test fails. I verified this by hand: applying the mutant to the committed code now fails the test (candidates drops from 4 to 3), and reverting it passes again.
